research_question: What mechanisms could explain subject-level variation in wearable stress-detection uncertainty?

stage_4_hypotheses.hypothesis: Individual differences in baseline autonomic tone cause systematic variation in wearable stress-detection uncertainty.
stage_4_hypotheses.proposed_mechanism: Subjects with higher resting parasympathetic activity exhibit lower heart-rate variability (HRV) signal-to-noise ratios, leading to noisier stress classifiers.
stage_4_hypotheses.core_assumption: Resting autonomic baseline is stable within a subject but varies substantially across subjects.
stage_4_hypotheses.knowledge_gap_addressed: Lack of quantitative linking between subject-level baseline autonomic metrics and model prediction uncertainty.

stage_4_hypotheses.hypothesis: Variability in sensor placement on the wrist introduces subject-specific measurement bias that propagates to uncertainty estimates.
stage_4_hypotheses.proposed_mechanism: Differences in radial artery depth and subcutaneous tissue thickness alter photoplethysmography (PPG) amplitude, causing heterogeneous signal quality across users.
stage_4_hypotheses.core_assumption: Users do not consistently wear the device at the same anatomical location across sessions.
stage_4_hypotheses.knowledge_gap_addressed: Insufficient characterization of how placement heterogeneity translates into per-subject predictive uncertainty.

stage_4_hypotheses.hypothesis: Physiological stress response heterogeneity (e.g., cortisol vs. sympathetic activation) leads to divergent wearable signal patterns across individuals.
stage_4_hypotheses.proposed_mechanism: Some subjects mount a primarily hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) response with minimal cardiac changes, while others show strong sympathetic surges, producing mismatched feature distributions for a single stress model.
stage_4_hypotheses.core_assumption: Stress phenotypes are categorical at the subject level and map onto distinct wearable signatures.
stage_4_hypotheses.knowledge_gap_addressed: Absence of subject-level stress phenotype mapping to wearable feature uncertainty.

stage_4_hypotheses.hypothesis: Temporal drift in sensor calibration (e.g., LED intensity decay) creates increasing uncertainty for long-term users.
stage_4_hypotheses.proposed_mechanism: Gradual degradation of optical components reduces PPG signal fidelity, inflating model prediction variance over weeks to months.
stage_4_hypotheses.core_assumption: Calibration drift is monotonic and subject-independent but its impact on uncertainty accumulates with usage duration.
stage_4_hypotheses.knowledge_gap_addressed: Limited longitudinal quantification of sensor aging effects on per-subject stress detection confidence.

stage_4_hypotheses.hypothesis: Self-report labeling noise varies by subject due to differences in emotional awareness and reporting latency.
stage_4_hypotheses.proposed_mechanism: Subjects with low interoceptive accuracy provide delayed or inaccurate stress timestamps, corrupting ground truth and inflating model uncertainty for those individuals.
stage_4_hypotheses.core_assumption: Labeling error is systematic per subject rather than random across the cohort.
stage_4_hypotheses.knowledge_gap_addressed: No existing model linking interoceptive ability metrics to wearable stress label reliability.

stage_4_hypotheses.hypothesis: Circadian phase at the time of measurement stratifies uncertainty because autonomic baseline shifts across the day.
stage_4_hypotheses.proposed_mechanism: Morning cortisol peaks and evening parasympathetic dominance alter HRV baselines, causing the same stressor to produce different feature deviations depending on time-of-day.
stage_4_hypotheses.core_assumption: Circadian modulation of autonomic features is consistent within a subject but varies across subjects.
stage_4_hypotheses.knowledge_gap_addressed: Lack of subject-specific circadian adjustment in uncertainty quantification for stress classifiers.

stage_4_hypotheses.hypothesis: Statistical model misspecification due to non-stationary noise processes yields subject-dependent uncertainty inflation.
stage_4_hypotheses.proposed_mechanism: Assuming i.i.d. Gaussian residuals ignores subject-specific autocorrelation in sensor noise (e.g., motion artifacts), leading to underestimation of predictive variance for high-mobility users.
stage_4_hypotheses.core_assumption: Noise autocorrelation structure differs across subjects and is not captured by the current model.
stage_4_hypotheses.knowledge_gap_addressed: Absence of subject-level noise modeling in wearable stress detection uncertainty estimates.

stage_4_hypotheses.hypothesis: Skin optical properties (melanin, thickness, hydration) modulate PPG signal quality, creating systematic per-subject uncertainty differences.
stage_4_hypotheses.proposed_mechanism: Higher melanin concentration attenuates green-light PPG, reducing signal-to-noise ratio and increasing classifier variance for darker-skinned individuals.
stage_4_hypotheses.core_assumption: Skin optical characteristics are stable within a subject and significantly affect wearable optical sensor performance.
stage_4_hypotheses.knowledge_gap_addressed: Insufficient empirical linking of dermatological metrics to per-subject stress detection uncertainty.

stage_4_hypotheses.hypothesis: Concurrent physical activity confounds stress detection differently across subjects based on habitual activity patterns.
stage_4_hypotheses.proposed_mechanism: Subjects who frequently engage in high-intensity exercise develop distinct motion artifact signatures that overlap with stress-induced autonomic changes, inflating uncertainty during active periods.
stage_4_hypotheses.core_assumption: Activity context distributions are subject-specific and not fully captured by generic activity classifiers.
stage_4_hypotheses.knowledge_gap_addressed: No subject-level activity-stress interaction model for uncertainty calibration.

stage_4_hypotheses.hypothesis: Genetic polymorphisms in autonomic regulation genes (e.g., ADRB1, COMT) cause inter-individual differences in wearable stress signal dynamics.
stage_4_hypotheses.proposed_mechanism: Variants affecting beta-adrenergic receptor sensitivity or catecholamine metabolism alter heart-rate response magnitude to stressors, leading to heterogeneous feature distributions and variable model confidence.
stage_4_hypotheses.core_assumption: Relevant genetic variants have measurable effect sizes on cardiac stress reactivity detectable by wearables.
stage_4_hypotheses.knowledge_gap_addressed: Lack of integration of genetic data into subject-specific uncertainty quantification for wearable stress detection.

stage_5_audits.decision_reason: Causal chain is questionable (higher parasympathetic activity does not necessarily lower HRV SNR), confounders not identified, and mechanism is generic (baseline physiology affecting model uncertainty applies broadly).
One critical check failed (confounders not identified), but mechanism is specific and testable; salvageable by identifying confounders such as skin tone, motion, device fit.
stage_5_audits.salvage_note: Add confounders: skin pigmentation, motion artifacts, device tightness, and ambient light; incorporate into model to isolate placement effect.

stage_5_audits.decision_reason: Confounders not identified; otherwise mechanism is specific and testable.
stage_5_audits.salvage_note: Identify confounders: stressor type, context, baseline fitness, time of day, and incorporate phenotype classification.

stage_5_audits.decision_reason: Mechanism is domain-generic (sensor drift affects all optical wearables similarly) and confounders not identified; not salvageable as a specific mechanism for stress detection uncertainty.
Confounders not identified; mechanism is specific to self-report labeling noise in stress detection.
stage_5_audits.salvage_note: Identify confounders: stressor intensity, context, recall bias, and mood; incorporate interoceptive accuracy as covariate.

stage_5_audits.decision_reason: Confounders not identified; mechanism is specific to circadian modulation of stress detection.
stage_5_audits.salvage_note: Identify confounders: chronotype, sleep quality, shift work, and individual circadian phase markers.

stage_5_audits.decision_reason: Mechanism is domain-generic (model misspecification due to non-stationary noise applies broadly) and confounders not identified.
Confounders not identified; mechanism is specific to skin optical properties affecting PPG-based stress detection.
stage_5_audits.salvage_note: Identify confounders: sensor contact pressure, ambient light, motion, skin hydration, and incorporate dermatological metrics.

stage_5_audits.decision_reason: Confounders not identified; mechanism is specific to activity-stress confounding in wearable stress detection.
stage_5_audits.salvage_note: Identify confounders: fitness level, exercise type, sensor location, and develop subject-specific activity models.

stage_5_audits.decision_reason: Confounders not identified; mechanism is specific to genetic polymorphisms affecting autonomic stress reactivity.
stage_5_audits.salvage_note: Identify confounders: population stratification, age, sex, fitness, medication, and incorporate principal components of genetic ancestry.
